gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 11 build entry now runs the gpio_wdt, bcm2835_wdt, and dw_wdt starter tests together with the dw_wdt survey gate so the simple-driver watchdog tranche stays reviewable in one place.

A dedicated survey gate now records that the dw_wdt starter, probe summary, and dedicated tests already exist while keeping the remaining registration-facing and platform-facing gaps explicit instead of letting the current scaffold overclaim parity.

The survey note now anchors the live dw_wdt lane to `master` `095bac327bb962d38a47555d20a2a647ef1cbd5b` so later runs can extend the same Phase 11 slice without rediscovering whether the platform-resource preflight already landed.

The bounded starter already derives fixed TOP timeout windows, mirrors reset-mode versus IRQ-mode timeout selection and pretimeout bookkeeping, and now exposes both a probe-time summary and a registration-facing handoff alongside register-image transitions without claiming platform-backed behavior.

Dedicated Phase 11 tests now keep fixed-top limits, custom-top ordering, probe-time bookkeeping, registration-facing watchdog info and parent handoff details, reset-mode and IRQ-mode timeout behavior, restart intent, and non-stoppable stop semantics reviewable around the landed starter.

The lane now records that include/uapi/linux/watchdog.h still owns struct watchdog_info plus the WDIOC_* and WDIOF_* or WDIOS_* surface, while include/linux/watchdog.h still owns watchdog_device and watchdog_ops so the DesignWare slice does not overclaim public-header or watchdog-core parity.
The slice note now records the exact starter contract so the repo does not blur the current in-memory driver model into clock, reset, IRQ, debugfs, or hardware-backed parity.

The starter now includes a tiny probe-time summary around fixed-versus-custom TOP sourcing, nowayout and restart-priority bookkeeping, stop-on-reboot intent, and already-running watchdog state before any platform-backed behavior lands.

The starter now includes a small registration-facing handoff that keeps watchdog info selection, parent linkage, driver-data setup, timeout-init intent, imported running-state bookkeeping, and register-device intent explicit before any live clock, reset, IRQ, or MMIO work.

The starter now includes a tiny platform-resource preflight around timer-clock choice, optional APB clock presence, reset-control availability, and optional pretimeout-IRQ wiring before any live devm calls or watchdog registration work lands.

Platform-driver registration, live clock and reset acquisition, IRQ registration, suspend and resume handling, debugfs support, devicetree TOP arrays, and live MMIO validation remain blocked until the lane grows beyond the landed registration handoff and platform-resource preflight into a hardware-validation plan.
